section_summary.extract_value: This section details the development and psychometric properties of a three-item life satisfaction scale. The scale measures satisfaction across socio-economic status, general health, and lifestyle, with scores ranging from 3 to 30. It demonstrated good psychometric properties, including a Cronbach's alpha of .769.
section_summary.evidence_source: 2.5.5 Life satisfaction As a measure of global life satisfaction, a three-item scale was specifically developed and used for the purpose of the study. Subjects had to rate how much they were satisfied with three dimensions respectively, regarding socio-economic status, general health status, and lifestyle and conditions, using a 10-point agreement scale. The score was calculated as the sum of items, ranging from 3 to 30. Higher scores mean better life satisfaction. The scale showed good psychometric properties, with a Cronbach's alpha of .769 and a one-factor solution explaining 68.70% of the overall variance.
